title: Standard Model particle identifications
purpose: Identify all 17 elementary particle types on one frozen candidate. Each species has a local preparation or production channel, reproducible detection statistics, and a dictionary that distinguishes its nearest alternatives. A declaration of a field or an input mass cannot identify the excitation.
reference: Count six quark flavours, three charged leptons, three active neutrino flavour channels, four gauge-boson types and the Higgs. W covers both signs, and the gluon entry covers the eight colour components. Resolve conjugate partners where distinct. Neutrino flavour is defined by weak production and detection; its propagation can mix mass eigenstates. Composite hadrons provide evidence for confined quarks and gluons. The hypothetical graviton has its own gravitational-particle assessment. A sterile neutrino is outside this inventory.

e.note: Two independent sources and two detectors identify the same charged winding state in free flight and at one resolved energy. Its contact charge is signed, its addressed winding rotation is orbital, and its clock line depends on the guide. A separate spinor shell requires repeated monitoring of prepared material heads. Intrinsic electron spin, electric flux and physical rest mass remain open. The lowest propagating band carries the winding code near a common guide threshold of 16 native units. After free flight a single negative charge carries three coherent winding amplitudes. Independent local phase and arm conventions reproduce ninety complete source and receiver banks. The conjugate windings have identical energy spectra. One terminal instrument couples each of the three arriving winding states to the same net-neutral pair, records donor compensation, and preserves the unknown winding. The full pulse gives conditional Schmidt-number-three fidelity lower bounds above 0.733 for both charge signs.

mu.note: Three mobile bound cores have incompatible rest and recoil hierarchies. A separate localized charged orbital demonstrably loses one native unit as a stocked neutral pair gains one unit in another owner. The emitting orbital lacks a physical muon mass and weak-flavor tag. The eight periodic guides with a common positive light threshold miss at least one of the two laboratory ratios by 29.2% or more across every triple of band minima. Every matched-host formation energy of the three-arm doublet apparatus lies between 8 and 27, excluding the laboratory hierarchy throughout that sector. On a twelve-port native vacancy, a common periodic drive produces three resolved clock rates. Their ratios approach 1, 206.770316 and 3477.472837 in the weak-drive limit at the programmed register phase. All three encoded states couple out during unforced evolution.

tau.note: The heaviest bound core measures 147.05535 against the 16-unit vacancy. families.name: Quarks
families.criterion: Recover the spin-half colour-triplet sector, its electric and weak responses, and a flavour discriminator in colour-singlet production, decay or scattering records. Resolve the conjugate sector.
types: Distinguish strangeness from light down flavour.
Identify charm production or weak transitions separately from up.
Resolve the heavy up-type resonance and its weak decay.

families.name: Charged leptons
families.criterion: Resolve spin half, unit negative charge, colour neutrality and weak interactions. Discriminate the three generations and their positive-charge conjugates through spectral or decay measurements.
types: Distinct mass and leptonic decay channel.
Third charged-lepton branch, with its weak decay channels.

families.name: Active neutrinos
families.criterion: Resolve a neutral spin-half weak sector, tag flavour by the accompanying charged lepton, and relate production, propagation and detection with the same mixing dictionary. Distinguish neutrino and antineutrino interaction channels where measurable.

families.name: Gauge bosons
families.criterion: Identify polarization, charge and the current coupled to the same propagating vector excitation.
types: Massless transverse electromagnetic response and its coupling to the measured electric current.
Colour-octet strong-current response and non-Abelian couplings in gauge-invariant signals.
Both signs of the massive charged weak vector and charged-current transitions.
Massive neutral weak vector, its polarizations and neutral-current couplings.

families.name: Scalar boson
families.criterion: Identify a neutral spin-zero resonance with independently distinguished couplings in the same electroweak sector.
types: Electroweak symmetry-breaking scalar and its characteristic production or decay responses.
